auth.notes: Account login in the app; session expiry forces re-login. Device registration is an account-scoped POST under users/{uuid}/product_registration. Not mapped further — none of it is on the local-control path.

data_leaves_device: Product registration record (device model/serial attached to the owner's account) — sent by the phone app, only on the stock registration route
Subscription entitlement state (server-side, via an external billing provider) — fetched and enforced by the app only; the F.REV.K firmware accepted Pro without it
cloud.failure_mode: The captured BLE settings operations require no cloud round trip, so an already-active unit retains its documented local controls when the vendor cloud is unavailable, Pro mode included (replay-confirmed 2026-11-14). Static analysis makes locked-unit activation locally constructible as well, but it was not directly verified. The cloud records product registration and supplies the entitlement state the stock app uses to gate Pro; complete registration-server behavior after the PEACH2 pre-connect API exception is not mapped.
cloud.notes: Monetization is a server-side subscription bought via an in-app web flow; the app has no in-app-purchase store integration. The subscription gates the app's Pro UI. Static analysis says an inactive subscription causes a Basic-mode write when the device reports Pro, and a separate testing flag bypasses that UI branch. The firmware itself does not check entitlement: a direct Pro write from a replacement client was accepted and persisted (2026-11-14). The downgrade path was not exercised. See `protocol_details.paywall`.
cloud.vendor_service: FOREO For You cloud (account, product-registration bookkeeping, subscription entitlement)

identity.notes: The security-access and activation writes both take bytes of the device's own BLE MAC, so the address is load-bearing for this protocol, not just an identity key. The advertisement carries the same MAC in its manufacturer data, which is the address-derived marker the stock app keys its activation-state check on. The value a locked unit advertises remains unknown — see `remaining_unknowns`.

methods.notes: The stock app disables fuzzy name matching and scans for the selected model's configured name for 30 seconds. Its scan handler also derives activation state from the raw advertisement. The active unit advertised manufacturer-specific data under company ID 0xFFFF whose payload is FF FF, the device's own 6-byte BLE MAC in printed order, then FF 01 (see `protocol_details.scan_to_add.activation_advertisement`). It carried no service UUIDs or service data.

identification.notes: App 4.4.1 and the 4.2.0 comparison build configure exact model-specific names: PEACH2, PEACH2GO, PEACH2Duo and PEACH2ProMAX. The spaced and trademark forms are retained as previously reported aliases, not as a reason to match every PEACH-prefixed device.

device.name: FOREO Peach 2 IPL hair removal
device.notes:
Mains-powered IPL (intense pulsed light) hair-removal device with BLE, Telink-based chipset, companion app FOREO For You. One spec covers the Peach 2 family — Peach 2, Peach 2 go, Peach 2 Pro MAX, Peach 2 Duo — which share one code path in the app and differ in command dialect (see `protocol_details.dialect_selection`) and in which UI modes the app exposes. Optical output up to 7.3 J/cm² with firmware skin-contact and eye-safety interlocks. IPL intensity is selected only on the handset's +/- buttons, per the vendor manuals; no BLE command sets it in the flows traced. What BLE does set is the removal mode (Basic, or Pro with its extra boost intensities), cooling, and on models that have one the T-Sonic vibration-motor level (FFF1 0A01, 0–5).
The device ships LOCKED: per the vendor manual it will not turn on until "registered" from the app. Static analysis derives the 0A20 activation payload entirely from the device's own BLE MAC (see `protocol_details.activation`), with no server input. That makes offline activation implementable in principle, but the locked-unit write was not observed: every unit examined was already active. PEACH2/GO/Pro Max also skip the stock app's pre-connect device-info lookup; account registration remains a separate later step.
Custom 16-bit UUIDs on the standard Bluetooth base (0000xxxx-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb). No pairing/bonding at any point (the app never bonds), no MTU negotiation on the Peach connect path — 20-byte writes suffice. No command framing: writes are raw opcode || payload, answers are read back from the command characteristic.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The activated captured unit advertised as PEACH2 and accepted bare connections. Whether a factory-locked unit advertises identically is still unverified.

exclusivity.notes: No SMP exchange or bonding occurred in either captured connection or in any of the seven replay connections (BlueZ reported Paired: no, Bonded: no). This does not establish how many centrals the peripheral accepts at once.
exclusivity.recovery: No bond exists to clear. If a connection stalls, close the vendor app and reconnect, then repeat the security-access write. Under BlueZ the first connect attempt frequently dropped during service discovery ("device disconnected"); an immediate retry succeeded every time. General single-central behavior remains unknown.

pairing.notes: No link-layer pairing occurred in either captured connection. What looks like security lives entirely above the link layer: the per-connection security-access write to 0A10 and, only on a locked unit, the activation write to 0A20. Both derive from the device's own BLE MAC. The first is capture- and replay-confirmed, though the active F.REV.K unit did not enforce it; the second remains app-derived because every unit examined was already active.

unpair.notes: Nothing to unpair: no bond was created in the capture, so moving to a new client needs no reset or forget-device step.

safety_advisory.detail: This is an IPL (intense pulsed light) hair-removal handset with an optical output up to 7.3 J/cm². Used wrongly it can cause permanent harm: burns, blistering, discoloration or scarring of the skin, and serious eye injury from looking into a flash. Always follow FOREO's own instructions — patch-test first, match the intensity level to your skin tone (darker skin needs a lower level), never treat broken, tanned, tattooed or moled skin, and keep it away from the eyes. This app only sets intensity and mode over Bluetooth; the flash itself is triggered on the device against its skin-contact interlock. This app is EXPERIMENTAL and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by FOREO — the manufacturer's manual and safety guidance govern.
safety_advisory.summary: IPL fires intense light pulses — improper use can cause permanent skin burns, blistering, scarring, or eye injury.

issued_to_client: Nothing. No keys, tokens or bonds are issued in either setup route; the cloud route's account session lives entirely in the phone app.
stored_on_device: Activation state derived from the device BLE MAC (0A20; the locked-unit write is app-derived)
Wake-up enable flag (0A30, only on firmware that exposes it; absent from the captured unit)

factory_reset.description: Nobody has established a reset procedure for the Peach 2. Static analysis describes activation as idempotent, so a second-hand unit should not need a reset for normal ownership. The locked-unit write remains unverified. Do not guess a procedure on an IPL device — the skin-contact and eye-safety interlocks make improvised button sequences a poor idea. Listed as `unknown` rather than `false` because nothing proves one does not exist.
factory_reset.effect: Not established. No factory-reset procedure was found in the app or in the manual text examined, and none occurred in the capture. What a reset would clear is unknown. Activation state (0A20) and wake-up (0A30, on firmware that exposes it) are the persisted setup state identified by static analysis; ordinary runtime-setting persistence was not established.

methods.description: Scan for the selected model's exact advertised name, connect without bonding, write the security-access handshake, then read 0A20 and, only if its first byte is 00, write 01 02 <8-byte chipId> as documented under `protocol_details.activation`. Read 0A30 and enable wake-up only on firmware that exposes that characteristic; the captured new-dialect unit did not expose it.
methods.name: Offline BLE activation (no account, no network)

steps.action: Plug in and scan for the selected model's exact configured name (PEACH2, PEACH2GO, PEACH2Duo or PEACH2ProMAX; the spaced/trademark aliases are retained in discovery). The stock app scans for 30 seconds.
steps.expect: Advertisement with the exact model name and manufacturer data (company ID 0xFFFF) carrying the device MAC and an activation-state byte (01 on an active unit). Do not treat every PEACH-prefixed device as this model.

steps.action: Connect (no bonding) and discover services. FFF0 contains FFF1, 0A10 and 0A20 on the captured firmware. The first connection attempt often drops during service discovery (4 of 7 replay sessions under BlueZ); retry the connect.
steps.expect: Connected with services resolved, usually by the second attempt.

steps.action: Write security access: 01 A1 <MAC[3]> <MAC[4]> <MAC[5]> to characteristic 0A10 (last three bytes of the device's own BLE MAC).
steps.expect: Write Response received; the stock app retries up to 3 times, waits 500 ms, and validates no challenge response before continuing. A 0A10 read afterwards returned 01 00 00 00 00 in the replay. On the active F.REV.K unit, FFF1 queries and writes also succeeded without this handshake, but send it anyway: whether a locked unit or other firmware enforces it is unknown.

steps.action: Read SW revision (2A28) — the device is ready; the value also selects the command dialect.
Read 0A20; if the value starts with byte 00, write 01 02 <chipId(MAC)> (see protocol_details.activation). If it already starts with 01, do not rewrite it.
steps.expect: Device unlocked; the already-active unit returned 01 (a 17-byte value whose remaining bytes are not decoded) in both the capture and the replay, and required no activation write.

steps.action: If 0A30 exists, read it and, unless the value starts with 01, write 01 (wake-up enabled). Skip this step when 0A30 is absent, as on the captured new-dialect unit.

cloud.local_alternative: The primary method above: the activation write is computable offline from the device's BLE MAC, so the cloud registration is optional end to end.

methods.description: The vendor flow: sign into a FOREO account in the app, which POSTs a product registration to the vendor cloud and then performs exactly the BLE activation above. The server call is warranty bookkeeping — none of its response feeds the unlock bytes — so this route adds an account and a network dependency without adding anything the firmware requires. Kept as documentation of what the stock app does, and the only route that records the unit under the owner's warranty account.
methods.name: Stock FOREO For You app registration

setup.notes: Nothing to provision — no network, no account. The one gate is the ship-lock: a factory-fresh Peach 2 refuses to operate until a client performs the BLE activation below. Static analysis shows the activation payload derives only from the device's own BLE MAC, so the offline route is primary. The 2026-11-07 capture and the 2026-11-14 replacement-client replay confirm discovery, security access, the SW-revision and 0A20 reads on an already-active unit; neither verifies the locked-unit write. PEACH2/GO/Pro Max skip the stock app's pre-connect device-information API lookup, but account registration is a separate later step whose complete server behavior is not mapped here.

rejoin.notes: There is no network to rejoin and no bond to move: a new phone just scans, connects and writes the security-access handshake. Only a unit whose 0A20 value is still locked needs the activation write.

testing.notes: 2026-11-14: an independent BlueZ + bleak client written from this spec alone drove an already-activated PEACH2 (SW revision PEACH2 F.REV.K) over seven connections. Driven and behaving as written: exact-name discovery, unbonded connect, a live GATT table matching `services` characteristic-for-characteristic (properties included), the 0A10 security-access write, DIS reads and dialect selection, the 0A20 read (01 = active, so no activation write), absence of 0A30, the 0A02 serial read, FFF1 queries 0B01 / 0BD0 / 0BC4 0007, write-backs of 0A01 and 0AD0 01 with 01-prefixed acknowledgements, a 0AD0 06 Pro write that read back 06 and persisted across reconnects, and 0A44 notifications, plus read-only 0BB2 / 0BB4 / 0BB5 / 0BD1 table queries, a T-Sonic write from 5 to 2 and back, and a handset check showing the IPL level is independent of 0A01. Not driven: the locked-unit activation write (no locked unit), 0A30 wake-up, cooling writes, any write to the 0AB*/0AD1 safety tables (deliberately), old-dialect and Duo paths, and OTA. Earlier evidence: the 2026-11-07 stock-app HCI capture of the same model.

artifacts.description: Static analysis of the FOREO For You app (2026-08). Source of every protocol fact here: the GATT map and the characteristic-by-UUID resolution, the command opcode table and dialect switch, the security-access handshake, the MAC-derived activation (chipId) algorithm, and the app-side-only subscription enforcement. A 2026-11-14 re-read established that FFF1 0A01 is the T-Sonic motor level (settings-screen wiring and the app's own opcode name), and recovered the per-firmware cooling profiles and Pro MAX IPL-speed tables from the app's bundled per-model settings config. Also establishes the negative findings: no bonding anywhere on the Peach path, no MTU negotiation, no in-app-purchase store integration, and no BLE command for the handset's IPL intensity in the settings flows.

Comparison build whose relevant PEACH2 implementations corroborate exact-name scanning, security access, subscription/test-device gating, Basic/Pro constants and Duo mode bytes. JADX reported 69 errors across the full bundle, so only the present matching implementations are used. No newer-store-version claim is made.

Cross-checks 27 writes/responses, 210 reads/responses and 517 notification packets. Identifies body/head NTC, accelerometer and vibrator-setting roles and their counts, exact scan behavior and the 500 ms post-security-access delay. Confirms seven Basic writes and no Pro write. Addresses, serials and raw security payloads are omitted.

Two connections to an already-active PEACH2 running PEACH2 F.REV.K. Confirms the FFF0 service map, MAC-derived security write, no-pairing session, 0A20 state 01, serial read from 0A02, intensity/mode writes, automatic fan and seven-byte cooling profile. Establishes the negative findings that 0A30, 0A07, Battery Service, TI OAD and D0FF were absent from this normal-mode table and 0A08 was read + notify. No locked-unit activation, Pro-mode write or OTA was captured. Real addresses, serial and activation values are not reproduced in this spec.

A standalone client written from this spec, importing no vendor code, drove an already-active PEACH2 (H.REV.C, SW PEACH2 F.REV.K) over seven connections. Confirmed: exact-name discovery and the manufacturer-data layout; no pairing; a live GATT table identical to `services`; the 0A10 handshake and its 01 00 00 00 00 read-back; dialect selection; 0A20 = 01 (no activation written); 0A30, 0A07 and 2A19 absent; the 14-byte 0A02 serial; 0B01 / 0BD0 / 0BC4 0007 queries; acknowledged write-backs of 0A01 05 and 0AD0 01; and a 0AD0 06 Pro write that read back 06 and persisted across reconnects, with no account or subscription. New negative findings: the 0A10 handshake is not enforced for FFF1 or 0A20 on this unit, and the first connect attempt dropped during service discovery in 4 of 7 sessions. The unit was left in Pro mode at the owner's request. MAC, serial and 0A20 trailing bytes are not reproduced here.

FOREO Peach 2, Peach 2 go and Peach 2 Pro Max user manuals (vendor-hosted, linked in helpful_urls). Corroborate the ship-locked behaviour and the registration requirement, and state that IPL intensity is chosen with the handset's +/- buttons, levels 1–3 being intended for sensitive areas and first-time users.

evidence.open_questions: `remaining_unknowns` now starts with a locked/factory-unit activation, then the handset's Pro-mode level range, old-dialect / Duo / Pro MAX behavior, sensor semantics and a safe OTA path. The FFF0 service, the new-dialect command envelope, the cooling level encoding, the T-Sonic role of 0A01 and firmware acceptance of Pro are settled by the 2026-11-07 capture, the 2026-11-14 replay and the bundled app config.

dfu_mode.notes: Static analysis expects the TI OAD service (f000ffc0) with Image Identify (ffc1) and Image Block (ffc2) after an update-mode reboot. That service was absent from the normal-mode capture, and its update-mode name and address remain unknown.

enter.notes: No verified entry command exists. Static analysis suggested a write to 00000a08, but the captured unit declares that characteristic read + notify and no OTA write was observed. Do not write 0A08 as an update trigger on this firmware.

image.notes: The app fetches images from the vendor's CDN; the fetch path is not recovered.

dfu.notes: App-derived, and thin: no transfer flow was traced, and whether app 4.4.1 can OTA a Peach at all is unconfirmed. Mechanism is left unknown rather than ti_oad because other vendors reuse these UUIDs over different stacks.

helpful_urls.description: Vendor-hosted online manual for the Peach 2. Corroborates the ship-locked behaviour and the in-app registration requirement this spec's activation flow replaces, and that IPL intensity is chosen on the handset's +/- buttons.
helpful_urls.title: FOREO PEACH 2 full user manual

helpful_urls.description: The companion app analysed for this spec (package com.foreo.foreoapp; analysed at 4.4.1 / versionCode 559 — the store listing always shows the current release).
helpful_urls.title: FOREO For You on Google Play

covers: Offline activation (unlock) of a factory-fresh unit — chipId derived from the device's BLE MAC, written to 0A20 (app-derived; every unit examined was already active)
Removal mode Basic/Pro set/read (0AD0/0BD0 on new firmware; 0AA2/0BA2 flash-mode bytes on old firmware) — Basic and Pro replay-confirmed with no subscription; old-firmware bytes app-derived
T-Sonic vibration-motor level set/read, 0–5 (0A01/0B01; the stock app shows it only when the model's settings config does not disable the motor)
Cooling/fan profile set/read (0AC4 seven-byte profile / 0BC4 0007; per-level profiles in protocol_details.cooling_profiles; 0AC0 0A automatic fan also captured)
Serial number (0A02 on the captured firmware) and SW revision (2A28); 0A07 and 2A19 were not present
Skin-sensor/accelerometer calibration polling (0A0C; one-byte read values captured, semantics unpinned)
Temperature-enable and head/body NTC threshold opcodes (0AB2/0AB4/0AB5 families; payload layouts unpinned — see remaining_unknowns)
not_covered: OTA firmware update — no safe entry or transfer is known. The captured 0A08 is read + notify, not a verified trigger write, and TI OAD was absent from normal-mode discovery
Firing flashes from the app is not a BLE operation on this device family in the flows traced — flashing is hardware-triggered against the skin-contact interlock
Selecting the IPL intensity level — done on the handset's +/- buttons per the vendor manuals; no BLE command for it was found in the flows traced
local_access.summary: Ordinary controls, Pro mode included, are fully local over BLE and were driven by a replacement client on 2026-11-14. Offline locked-unit activation is implementable from static analysis but not hardware-confirmed; do not treat it as a verified capability.

activation.chip_id_algorithm:
chipId is a fixed, keyless permutation of the 6-byte BLE MAC (m0 m1 m2 m3 m4 m5, in the usual printed order). Let b = [m5, m4, m3, 0x00, 0x00, m2, m1, m0]. Then the 8 output bytes are (all arithmetic mod 256):

  out[0] = (b[2] & 0x0F) | (b[7] & 0xF0)
  out[1] = (b[5] & 0x0F) | (b[1] & 0xF0)
  out[2] = (b[7] & 0x0F) + (0xF0 - (b[6] & 0xF0))
  out[3] = 0xFF - b[6]
  out[4] = b[5] + 1
  out[5] = (b[1] & 0x0F) + (0xF0 - (b[2] & 0xF0))
  out[6] = (b[0] & 0x0F) | (b[5] & 0xF0)
  out[7] = (b[6] & 0x0F) | (b[0] & 0xF0)

No key, no nonce, no server input — pure MAC arithmetic. `scripts/test_foreo_peach2_spec.py` transcribes this algorithm and asserts the vectors below.
activation.description: Run after every connect: (1) security access — write 01 A1 <MAC[3]> <MAC[4]> <MAC[5]> to 0A10 (retried up to 3x by the stock app); (2) read SW revision 2A28; (3) read 0A20 and only if its first byte is 00 write 01 02 <8-byte chipId>; (4) only when 0A30 exists, read it and unless its first byte is 01 write 01. The captured unit was already active, exposed no 0A30, and instead proceeded to read its serial from 0A02. Steps 1–2 and the 0A20 read are capture- and replay-confirmed; the locked-unit activation write and 0A30 flow are app-derived.

test_vectors.description: Documentation MAC 00:11:22:33:44:55-style placeholder (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF) — identifies no real unit. A client whose chipId(MAC) does not reproduce these bytes has mis-transcribed the algorithm.

vectors.step: chipId (payload of the 01 02 … activation write to 0A20)

capture_verified_vectors.meaning: Seven-byte current cooling profile (the F.REV.I–K level-0 profile); the remainder of the 18-byte response was zero.
Set T-Sonic motor level 3; subsequent 18-byte read-back began 01.
Set the F.REV.I–K level-1 cooling profile (see cooling_profiles).
Accepted after calibration polling, with the usual 01-prefixed read-back. Its semantics are unknown; do not generalize it into a calibration command.

command_protocol.framing: No framing: no header, length or checksum. Writes to FFF1 are raw `opcode || payload`. First byte 0A = write/set, 0B = read/query; second byte = sub-opcode.
command_protocol.query_model: Write `0B xx` to FFF1, then READ FFF1 back and parse the returned bytes. A read-back of all FF bytes means the device was busy; the app retries up to 5 times. Every write is verified by the same read-back. The observed settings-write acknowledgement was 18 bytes beginning 01 and otherwise zero. A busy reply to a write means it was not applied: re-send the write, not just the read.
command_protocol.read_back_formats: The T-Sonic motor level is the first byte of the 0B01 read-back (05 observed); removal mode 01 means Basic and >= 6 means Pro (0BD0; 06 observed after 0AD0 06). The new 0BC4 0007 query returned an 18-byte value whose first seven bytes are the cooling profile accepted by 0AC4. 0BB2 returns one byte and 0BB4 / 0BB5 / 0BD1 return their tables as leading bytes followed by zeros (replay-confirmed on F.REV.K). The 0BA2 layout remains unpinned.

replay_verified_vectors.description: Driven by a replacement client on 2026-11-14 against an active PEACH2 F.REV.K; 18-byte read-backs abbreviated to their non-zero prefix.

vectors.meaning: T-Sonic level 5 written back unchanged; acknowledged with or without the 0A10 handshake.
Pro removal mode accepted with no subscription or account.
Pro read back immediately and again after a fresh connection.
Ten-entry flash voltage table, read in Pro mode; read only.
Head-NTC thresholds 55 / 50, matching the app's model config.
Body-NTC thresholds 80 / 70, matching the app's model config.
Temperature-enable 02, matching the app's model config.
T-Sonic level lowered from 5 to 2; 0B01 then read 02.

cooling_profiles.description: The stock app's cooling control maps levels 0–5 to fixed seven-byte 0AC4 profiles chosen by SW revision (2A28). Older firmware uses the single-byte 0AC0 path; F.REV.L and the Pro MAX use eight-byte rows whose last byte carries the level. Pick the row for the unit's exact SW revision; do not interpolate. Values are hex.
cooling_profiles.level_encoding: In every table the level appears as a percentage: 00/23/32/41/50/64 hex (0/35/50/65/80/100 %) or 14/28/3C/50/64 hex (20/40/60/80/100 %), with 22 1B… standing in for level 0 on F.REV.I–K. The fixed bytes are not decoded.

tables.note: Eight bytes, while set_cooling documents seven; these firmwares were not examined on hardware.

cooling_profiles.verification_note: Table taken from the stock app's bundled per-model settings config. The F.REV.I–K level-0, level-1 and level-5 rows match bytes seen on hardware (capture and replay); the rest are app-derived.

dialect_selection.description: Two command dialects exist. Peach 2 go and Pro MAX use the NEW dialect; Duo has a separate mode-command path using repeated 0AA2 bytes even though the broader new-dialect family rules apply to it. A plain Peach 2 uses the OLD dialect when the last character of its SW revision string (2A28) is in a–c, otherwise the new dialect. Old vs new differs in removal/flash mode (0AA2 flash-mode bytes vs 0AD0 removal mode) and cooling (0AC0 vs 0AC4, 0BC0 vs 0BC4 0007). Duo Basic is 0AA2 02 02 02 02 02 and Duo Pro is 0AA2 03 03 03 03 03; neither was captured, and the Duo Pro switch is hidden in the app. The captured PEACH2 F.REV.K unit used 0AD0/0BC4 and also accepted 0AC0 0A auto-fan.
dialect_selection.verification_note: One new-dialect unit is capture-confirmed; the old-dialect suffix rule and other suffix edge cases remain app-derived.

ipl_speed.description: Pro MAX only (bundled config for PEACH2ProMAX F.REV.A–F): an "IPL speed" setting with Fast and Balanced modes on FFF1 opcode 0AA3, read back with 0BA3 0A. Each mode is a fixed set of seven write strings of the form 0AA3 <n> <n non-increasing per-step bytes>, for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 10. Fast starts each table at 0D, Balanced at 0A–0C. What n and the step bytes control is not decoded, and nothing in this family was examined on hardware. Not applicable to the plain PEACH2, whose config has no IPL-speed entry.

paywall.enforcement: The only gate is in the app, before the settings write. Once the app permits Pro, it writes 0AD0 06 to FFF1; Basic is 0AD0 01. There is no token, key or server-issued blob anywhere on the Pro path, and the firmware does not enforce entitlement: on 2026-11-14 a replacement client with no FOREO account wrote 0AD0 06 to a PEACH2 F.REV.K, which acknowledged it, read back 06, and still reported 06 after a fresh connection. Static analysis says the stock app, on connecting to a non-Duo device that reports >= 6 while it considers the subscription inactive, writes Basic back, so opening the stock app undoes the change; that downgrade was not exercised. Security access on 0A10 is connection setup, not a Pro unlock token. Basic mode, cooling and the T-Sonic level are not paywalled. The Basic/Pro switch is shown for Peach 2 go / Pro MAX always and for a plain Peach 2 on new firmware (SW revision not ending in a–g); it is hidden on Duo. Duo uses repeated 0AA2 mode bytes instead of 0AD0; its Pro command was not captured either. 'Peach 2 Pro MAX' is a separate hardware SKU.
gated_features: Pro removal mode and its five additional boost intensities (Peach 2 family UI)
paywall.mechanism: Server-side subscription (via an external billing provider), bought through an in-app web flow — the app has no in-app-purchase store integration. Entitlement is fetched from the vendor API, cached locally and checked in the UI. Normal Pro selection requires both the subscription flag and an active subscription state. A separate testing == 1 flag bypasses the inactive-subscription UI branch; that is a vendor-test exception, not an ordinary registration requirement.
paywall.verification_note: Firmware acceptance of a direct Pro write is replay-confirmed on one PEACH2 F.REV.K. The app-side gate and downgrade logic are app-derived; Duo and old-dialect Pro paths are untested.

activation_advertisement.capture_value: 01 (active unit); the locked-unit value is unobserved
activation_advertisement.note: Inactive and OTA devices are published immediately; already-active devices are accumulated for later filtering. That the trailing byte reads 00 on a locked unit is inferred from the app logic, not observed.
activation_advertisement.observed_layout: Manufacturer-specific data, company ID 0xFFFF (little-endian FF FF on air), payload FF FF <MAC m0..m5> FF 01 — e.g. for the documentation MAC AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF the payload would read FF FF AA BB CC DD EE FF FF 01. The MAC is the address-derived marker; the final byte, 01 on an already-active unit, is the likely activation nibble. Observed 2026-11-14 on an active PEACH2 F.REV.K.
activation_advertisement.source: Raw scan record, using an address-derived marker and a following nibble ending in 1 or 0

scan_to_add.registration: The three named models skip the stock app's pre-connect device-info API lookup and publish the scanned device directly. Account registration is a separate later step, not something this exception proves unnecessary.

security_access.role: Connection setup, not a Pro token, activation write or IPL firing command. On the active F.REV.K unit FFF1 queries and writes worked without it.

remaining_unknowns: Locked/factory-unit behavior: the advertisement's trailing activation byte on a locked unit (01 on an active one), whether locked units accept security access immediately or enforce it, and whether they accept the documented 01 02 chipId write. Every unit examined was already active.
Complete registration/server behavior after the PEACH2/GO/Pro Max pre-connect API exception; the exception itself does not prove registration is unnecessary.
0A30 wake-up, 0A07 chip ID and 2A19 battery were absent from the captured new-dialect GATT table; their presence and containing services on other firmware remain unknown.

The fixed (non-level) bytes of the 0AC4 cooling profiles, whether F.REV.L / Pro MAX accept their eight-byte rows and how 0BC4 0007 reports the eighth byte; the 0BA2 read-back layout; what the Pro MAX 0AA3 IPL-speed bytes control.

How Pro's 'five extra boost intensities' are applied. The handset still offers five levels in Pro (owner observation, 2026-11-14) and the flash voltage table holds ten entries, so levels 1–5 most likely select entries 6–10 in Pro; confirming that needs a 0BD1 read in Basic and an observation of which entry a flash uses, neither done. Units of the voltage entries are unknown.

Whether any BLE command sets or reads the handset's IPL intensity. None was found in the app's Peach settings flows, and 0A01/0B01 is ruled out on hardware (the handset level changed with 0B01 unchanged).
Whether a handshake-less connection can do anything the handshake normally gates. On the active F.REV.K unit nothing tested required it.
Units and conversion formulas for body/head NTC (0A18/0A19), accelerometer axes/units (0A0C), the vibrator-setting vocabulary (0A0D), the unknown 0A44/0A09 streams, and the accepted 0AB1 A5 write.
Old-dialect behavior, Duo-specific mode/cooling paths and SW-revision suffix edge cases beyond the one confirmed new-dialect F.REV.K unit; Duo Pro was not captured.

Whether the stock app's downgrade-to-Basic actually fires on connect, and whether other firmware revisions, the Pro MAX or the Duo also accept Pro without entitlement. Only one F.REV.K unit was tested.
OTA entry, image fetch/transfer, update-mode identity and recovery. The captured 0A08 is read + notify, so the earlier write-trigger hypothesis is not valid for this unit.

Whether the peripheral accepts only one central at a time; short sequential connections do not establish a general exclusivity rule. Also why the first BlueZ connect attempt so often drops during service discovery.
Whether any model exposes a remote-fire command. None was identified in the reviewed app flows or this capture, which is a scoped negative result, not proof of absence.
FOREO Bear 2 (microcurrent, same app) appears to share the activation + subscription pattern per code structure — follow-up target if a unit is acquired

get_body_ntc_threshold.description: Body-NTC threshold read; the leading non-zero bytes are the threshold list. The replay read 50 46 (80, 70), matching the app's model config; units not established.

get_cooling.description: Read cooling level on OLD firmware (0BC0).

get_cooling_new.description: Read the new-firmware cooling profile (0BC4 0007). The first seven bytes are the profile accepted by set_cooling; the observed read-back was 18 bytes. The replay read 64 0D 21 02 1C 14 14, the F.REV.K level-5 profile.

get_flash_voltage_table.description: Flash voltage table read. In Pro mode on F.REV.K the replay read ten entries, 06 0A 0F 15 19 18 1B 1D 20 23, then zeros. Units are not established. The handset still offers five levels in Pro (owner observation), so the likely reading is that levels 1–5 use entries 1–5 in Basic and entries 6–10 (the app's "5 extra boost intensities") in Pro. That mapping is a hypothesis; see remaining_unknowns.

get_head_ntc_threshold.description: Head-NTC threshold read; the leading non-zero bytes are the threshold list. The replay read 37 32 (55, 50), matching the app's model config; units not established.

get_removal_mode.description: Read removal mode; a read-back value >= 6 means Pro. Basic returned 01 in the capture and the replay; Pro returned 06 in the replay.

get_temperature_enable.description: Temperature-enable read; the first byte of the read-back is the setting. The replay read 02 on F.REV.K, matching the app's model config.

get_tsonic_level.description: Read the T-Sonic motor level; the level is the first byte of the FFF1 read-back (05 in both the capture and the replay).

set_auto_fan.description: Enable automatic fan control (0AC0 0A). Accepted on the captured new-dialect unit as well as documented for the old dialect.

set_body_ntc_threshold.advanced_reason: Moves a thermal cut-out threshold on an IPL handset. Do not write it.
set_body_ntc_threshold.description: Body-NTC threshold set: 0AB5 followed by the threshold list, one byte per entry. Same check-and-rewrite pattern as the head threshold. No executable template, deliberately.

set_cooling.advanced_reason: Cooling protects the skin during flashing. Send only one of the stock per-level profiles for the unit's SW revision (protocol_details.cooling_profiles); do not substitute arbitrary bytes on an IPL device.
set_cooling.description: New-firmware cooling profile write: 0AC4 followed by exactly seven bytes. The stock app does not compose these bytes: it picks one of six fixed per-level profiles from its bundled model config, keyed by SW revision (see `protocol_details.cooling_profiles`). On F.REV.I–K the first byte is the cooling level as a percentage (14/28/3C/50/64 hex = 20–100 % for levels 1–5) and 22 1B… is level 0. The other fields are fixed per firmware family and not decoded.

profile.description: The cooling row for the unit's SW revision from protocol_details.cooling_profiles: seven bytes on F.REV.D–K and PEACH2GO F.REV.B–C (capture-confirmed on F.REV.K), eight bytes on PEACH2 F.REV.L, PEACH2GO F.REV.D and Pro MAX F.REV.A–B, where the eighth byte carries the level (app config only; those firmwares were not examined, and how get_cooling_new reports the eighth byte is unknown). Read-back carries the profile followed by zeroes.

set_cooling_old.advanced_reason: Writes an arbitrary cooling byte to an IPL device's old-firmware cooling path; the value meanings are not decoded beyond set_auto_fan's 0A. Cooling protects the skin during flashing, so prefer set_auto_fan.
set_cooling_old.description: OLD-firmware single-byte cooling write (0AC0); use set_auto_fan for the documented automatic mode.

set_flash_mode.advanced_reason: Changes the flash mode of an IPL device (Face, Basic or Pro) on the old-firmware and Duo paths only, none of which were captured. Sent to the wrong dialect it is an unverified write; check protocol_details.dialect_selection and read the mode back with get_flash_mode.
set_flash_mode.description: OLD-firmware flash mode and the separate Duo mode-command path; the mode byte is repeated five times (Basic = 02 x5, Pro = 03 x5, Face = 01 x5). Other new-firmware models use set_removal_mode_* instead — see `protocol_details.dialect_selection`. Duo Pro was not captured.

set_flash_voltage_table.advanced_reason: Directly sets flash energy per intensity level on an IPL device. Raising it can exceed the output the skin-tone and eye-safety design assumes and cause burns or eye injury. Read only; never write.
set_flash_voltage_table.description: Flash voltage table set: 0AD1 followed by the per-level table, one byte per entry. The stock app reads 0BD1 on connect and rewrites the table from its server-delivered model config when the read-back does not start with it. This is FOREO's energy calibration, not a user setting, and it is the only per-level energy control found: there is no BLE command for the handset level itself. No executable template, deliberately. The five-entry table in the app's bundled offline config is stale (that entry is marked deleted, and the live unit holds ten entries), so never "restore" it.

set_head_ntc_threshold.advanced_reason: Moves a thermal cut-out threshold on an IPL handset; a wrong value can let the treatment head overheat against skin. Do not write it.
set_head_ntc_threshold.description: Head-NTC (temperature) threshold set: 0AB4 followed by the threshold list, one byte per entry, as the app's config holds it. The app rewrites it on connect when 0BB4 differs. No executable template, deliberately.

set_removal_mode_pro.advanced_reason: Switches an IPL device to its higher-output Pro removal mode, which unlocks boost intensities above the Basic range on the handset. Pro is for non-sensitive body areas and experienced users; read the mode back with get_removal_mode, patch-test, and match the handset intensity to your skin tone per the vendor manual.
set_removal_mode_pro.description: New-firmware removal mode: Pro, which the app describes as five extra boost intensities for experienced users and recommends for non-sensitive body areas. The stock app permits this write only with an active eligible subscription or its testing flag, but the firmware does not check: on 2026-11-14 a replacement client with no account wrote it to a PEACH2 F.REV.K, got the usual 01 acknowledgement, read back 06, and still read 06 after reconnecting. The stock app writes Basic back on its next connect if it considers the subscription inactive.

set_temperature_enable.advanced_reason: Changes the handset's temperature-protection setting, a safety parameter the vendor pushes from its model config. Never write a value other than the one the unit already reports.
set_temperature_enable.description: Temperature-enable set: 0AB2 followed by one byte. The stock app reads 0BB2 on connect and, if the value differs from its model config, writes the config value back. Deliberately given no executable template here.

set_tsonic_level.description: Set the T-Sonic vibration-motor level, 0–5. This is the handset's massage motor, not IPL output: the app's own name for the opcode is "motor level", and the settings screen shows it under a T-Sonic heading. Hardware agrees (2026-11-14): with 0A01 set to 2 the handset showed one IPL dot, and pressing + moved it to two dots while 0B01 still read 02, so the handset IPL level neither follows nor is reported by this opcode. Earlier revisions of this spec called it IPL intensity, which was wrong.

characteristics.name: Command channel
characteristics.notes: All Peach commands are written here and all answers read back from the same characteristic. First byte 0A = write/set, 0B = read/query; second byte = sub-opcode. Dialect selection is in `protocol_details.dialect_selection`.

characteristics.name: Direct characteristic 0A01 (role unverified)
characteristics.notes: Separate from the 0A01 T-Sonic opcode on FFF1. Present in live GATT but not used in the capture or the replay.

characteristics.name: Serial number
characteristics.notes: The stock app read a 14-byte ASCII serial here. No write was attempted; the unit-specific value is deliberately not retained in this spec.

security_access.description: Handshake: 01 A1 followed by the last three bytes of the device's own BLE MAC (printed order m0..m5; send m3 m4 m5).

mac3.description: Byte 3 of the device BLE MAC (4th printed octet).

mac4.description: Byte 4 of the device BLE MAC.

mac5.description: Byte 5 of the device BLE MAC (last octet).

characteristics.name: Security access
characteristics.notes: Session handshake, written once after service discovery; the stock app retries the write up to 3 times. The live write matched the MAC-derived construction exactly. GATT also declares read access, which the earlier app-only map omitted; the replay read 01 00 00 00 00 after a successful write. Not enforced on the active F.REV.K unit: FFF1 queries, the 0A20 read and settings writes all succeeded on a connection that never wrote 0A10. Clients should still send it, since locked units and other firmware are untested.

characteristics.name: Sensor notifications 0A44
characteristics.notes: Frequent one-byte notifications were captured; their physical meaning is not decoded. The replay saw D0/D1 values, three in five seconds on an idle unit.

characteristics.name: Notifications 0A08 (role unverified)
characteristics.notes: Live properties are read + notify, not the OTA-trigger write inferred from app constants. No OTA operation was captured. Do not write this characteristic as an update trigger on this firmware.

characteristics.name: Body NTC notifications
characteristics.notes: The app identifies this as body NTC. The capture contains 165 one-byte notifications even though the declaration omits the notify property; units and conversion are undecoded.

characteristics.name: Sensor notifications 0A09
characteristics.notes: Thirteen one-byte notifications were captured; their semantics are undecoded.

characteristics.name: Head NTC notifications
characteristics.notes: The app identifies this as head NTC. The capture contains 110 one-byte notifications even though the declaration omits the notify property; units and conversion are undecoded.

characteristics.name: Accelerometer polling
characteristics.notes: The app names this accelerometer input and repeatedly read 180 one-byte values during calibration; axes, units and thresholds remain undecoded.

characteristics.name: Vibrator setting notifications
characteristics.notes: The app names this vibrator setting. Fifteen one-byte notifications were captured; the value vocabulary is undecoded.

activate.advanced_reason: Unlocks a locked IPL device in place of the vendor's own registration flow; the write was never captured (the captured unit was already active). Send it only after reading 0A20 and seeing a first byte of 00, never to an active unit.
activate.description: Unlock a locked unit: 01 02 followed by the 8-byte chipId derived from the device's BLE MAC (keyless permutation, fully offline — see `protocol_details.activation`).

chip_id.description: 8-byte chipId = keyless nibble permutation of the 6-byte BLE MAC; algorithm and test vectors in protocol_details.activation.

characteristics.name: Activate (unlock/register)
characteristics.notes: Read first: static analysis says a first byte of 00 means locked. The captured unit returned 01 and therefore received no activation write; the replay read the same 01 as the first byte of a 17-byte value whose trailing bytes are unit-specific and not decoded (not reproduced here). The read succeeded with or without the 0A10 handshake. The locked-unit write and its chipId derivation remain reported, not hardware-confirmed. (Other FOREO models use an older 01 01 <ASCII serial> variant; Peach uses the chip-id variant.)

services.name: FOREO Peach Command and Security Service
services.notes: Live service discovery on 2026-11-07 confirmed this containing service and every characteristic below; the 2026-11-14 replay found the same table with identical properties. The earlier stand-in 0A20 service was wrong. All command traffic is raw `opcode || payload` with no header, length or checksum; queries are written and then answered by READING FFF1 back. A read-back of all FF bytes means the device was busy — the app retries up to 5 times, and in the replay roughly one write in five returned busy and succeeded on the next try. Every accepted settings write was followed by an 18-byte read-back whose first byte was 01.

characteristics.name: Direct characteristic 0A05 (role unverified)
characteristics.notes: The stock app did not read or write this characteristic. Do not confuse it with the serial number read from 0A02 on the captured firmware.

services.name: FOREO 0x181C service
services.notes: Present beside FFF0 in the captured GATT table; no 0x180F Battery Service was present on this unit.

services.name: Device Information Service
services.notes: Standard DIS. SW revision (2A28) is read at every connect and selects the old/new command dialect (see protocol_details.dialect_selection). The captured unit reported PEACH2 F.REV.K and therefore used the new dialect.

services.name: TI OAD (Over-the-Air Download)
services.notes: Present in the app with image characteristics …ffc1 and …ffc2, but not present in the captured unit's normal-mode GATT table. It may require a separate update mode; no trigger or transfer was captured. Whether app 4.4.1 can OTA a Peach remains unconfirmed.

services.name: Unidentified D0FF service (declared, apparently unused)
services.notes: Declared in the app but absent from the captured normal-mode GATT table. No use was found in 4.4.1 or observed live. Its role is unconfirmed; leave it alone rather than probing it as OTA.
